content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E043 (Karen Sloan) requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes from HR and Security:
- HR says: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation admin. HR believes admin is permitted since role owns system.
- Security says: role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Security says contractors never get admin, basic training means write not permitted, max read. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.

Conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor. Also HR says admin, Security says read.

The policy says:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Who to trust? The Security agent's note references the Security DB which tracks employment type. HR may have wrong info. Typically in these tasks, the Security agent info is authoritative for employment type? The conflict matters. The recommended decision in Security note: grant read.

Also note HR says role owns Payroll system (Payroll Specialist), so if full-time, admin would be allowed. But Security says contractor, so never admin.

The max would be read (contractor, basic training). Requested admin exceeds max, so grant max = read.

Which note to trust? Security DB is more reliable for employment status. The Security agent gave the coherent policy-based reasoning. I'll go with read.

Let me submit decision: read.
